_status: Learner guide, Try it 1.2B and its answers (19 October 2026). Case wording follows the deck slide.

items.text: A beneficiary list with ID numbers shared as a public spreadsheet link.
items.reason: Anyone with the link can see ID numbers. If the link was opened by people with no right to it, this is likely a notifiable breach.

items.text: Payroll emailed to a personal address to work from home.
items.reason: Personal email is outside the office's control and its access rules; payroll data may include sensitive information.

items.text: A laptop with unencrypted HR files stolen from a car.
items.reason: Data taken off-site must be encrypted (Sec. 23). With sensitive HR data and likely harm, the 3S test points to notification.

items.text: A vendor given full database access with no written agreement.
items.reason: The office stays responsible for what its vendors do (Secs. 14 and 21). The vendor needs a written agreement that sets its duties, and only the access its job needs.

items.text: Citizen letters pasted into a free public chatbot.
items.reason: Not compliant, unless the tool is approved and the personal data is removed first. Pasting letters into a public tool discloses them to a third party.

items.text: A defaced website on a server holding no personal data.
items.reason: Without personal data it is not a personal data breach, so there is no NPC notice. It is still a security incident: document it, fix it, check other systems, and report it under DICT's reporting mechanism.
